 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Dr. Umesh Manshore - Advocate for the applicant.
Shri Viraj Godha - G.A. for the State.
ORDER 1.
They are heard.
Perused the charge sheet.

2. This is the first application under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 / 439 of Criminal Procedure Code,
1973, as he / she is implicated in connection with Crime No.02/2024 registered at Police Station Mandav, District Dhar (MP) for offence punishable under Section 363, 366, 376(3), 376(2)(n) of IPC and 3/4(2) and 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in custody since 30/12/2024.
3. The allegation against the applicant is of abduction and rape.

4. Counsel for the applicant has submitted that admittedly the prosecutrix was a consenting party and resided with the applicant for around seven and half months and she has also been examined in the trial Court and has not supported the case of the prosecution, copy of her deposition has also been filed on record and the age of the prosecutrix is also in dispute.
It is further submitted that the applicant is lodged in jail since 18/07/2024 and the final conclusion of trial is likely to take sufficient long time.
Hence, it is submitted that the bail application be allowed and he be released on bail.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 5. Counsel for the respondent / State, on the other hand has opposed the prayer submitting that the case diary is not available and it is submitted that no case for grant of bail is made out.

6. Having considered the rival submissions and on perusal of the charge sheet available with the counsel for the applicant as also the deposition of the prosecutrix, and taking note of the fact that the applicant is lodged in jail since 18/07/2024, age of the prosecutrix is in dispute and final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficient long time, in the considered opinion of this Court,
the applicant's application deserves to be allowed.
7. Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application filed by the applicant is allowed.

The applicant is directed to be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/-
(rupees twenty five thousand) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his/her regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he / she shall remain present before the court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
Certified copy as per rules.
